title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
description: Ten documented Smith College rituals that mark the academic year, community gatherings and commencement.

cards.title: Begin the year in John M. Greene Hall
cards.subtitle: Formal opening of the college year
cards.notes: Look for the opening address and Glee Club performance held for entering students and faculty before classes begin.
cards.short_summary: Smith’s formal first gathering of the academic year.
cards.evidence_claim: Smith identifies President’s Welcome Assembly as the formal beginning of the college year, with first-year students, faculty, an opening address and Glee Club performance.
cards.access_notes: Program details are announced by Smith for each academic year.

cards.title: Wait for the bells to declare a fall holiday
cards.subtitle: Surprise autumn break from classes
cards.notes: Listen for the college bells on a fall day; Smith’s president announces the surprise break, then students choose their own daytime plans.
cards.short_summary: A bell-signaled fall holiday that dates to 1877.
cards.evidence_claim: Smith says Mountain Day is a surprise break from classes announced by the president ringing the college bells; the first was held in 1877.
cards.access_notes: The date is not fixed; Smith announces it on a suitable fall day.

cards.title: Attend the Cromwell Day program
cards.subtitle: Annual programs honoring Otelia and Adelaide Cromwell
cards.notes: Check Smith’s annual schedule for workshops, lectures, films and entertainment honoring Otelia Cromwell and Adelaide Cromwell.
cards.short_summary: A campus-wide day of learning and reflection.
cards.evidence_claim: Smith describes Cromwell Day as an annual slate of workshops, lectures, films and entertainment honoring Otelia Cromwell, class of 1900, and Adelaide Cromwell ’40.
cards.access_notes: Morning and afternoon classes are canceled so students can attend the scheduled events.

cards.title: Find Julia Child Day at dinner
cards.subtitle: Thursday before Thanksgiving
cards.notes: Visit a campus dining hall on the Thursday before Thanksgiving to see the annual dinner honoring alumna Julia McWilliams Child ’34.
cards.short_summary: A dining tradition celebrating Smith’s famed cookbook-author alumna.
cards.evidence_claim: Smith says Julia Child Day occurs on the Thursday before Thanksgiving and features Julia Child’s recipes across campus dining halls for dinner.
cards.access_notes: Campus dining access and menu details are determined by Smith for the annual observance.

cards.title: Spot seniors’ creative hats and first regalia
cards.subtitle: Annual all-college convocation
cards.notes: Follow the annual convocation announcement and look for seniors wearing graduation robes for the first time, often with creative hats.
cards.short_summary: A February gathering with Smith College Medals and senior regalia.
cards.evidence_claim: Smith calls Rally Day an annual tradition where distinguished alums receive Smith College Medals and seniors first wear graduation regalia, often with creative hats.
cards.access_notes: Smith schedules Rally Day annually in February; consult the current event page for attendance details.

cards.title: See the graduating class plant ceremonial ivy
cards.subtitle: Day-before-Commencement procession
cards.notes: During Commencement Weekend, watch the senior procession and ceremonial ivy planting that symbolizes graduates’ connection to Smith.
cards.short_summary: A century-plus commencement rite rooted in the Class of 1884.
cards.evidence_claim: Smith states that Ivy Day has been a tradition for more than a century; the Class of 1884 first planted ivy as part of its graduation ceremonies.
cards.source_title: Commencement & Ivy Day Traditions | Smith College
cards.access_notes: Held on the day before Commencement as part of Smith’s graduation weekend.

cards.title: See the campus glow with colored lanterns
cards.subtitle: Commencement Weekend evening tradition
cards.notes: Return at dusk during Commencement Weekend to view colored paper lanterns and major-building light displays across campus.
cards.short_summary: A lantern-lit evening for graduating students to reflect together.
cards.evidence_claim: Smith says Illumination Night lights the campus with colored paper lanterns and fanciful light displays on some major buildings.
cards.source_title: Commencement & Ivy Day Traditions | Smith College
cards.access_notes: Occurs during Commencement Weekend; confirm the current weekend program before visiting.

cards.title: Watch reunion classes parade in white
cards.subtitle: Ivy Day procession tradition
cards.notes: During reunion weekend, look for alumnae classes in white, differentiated by colored ribbons and carrying class placards in the parade.
cards.short_summary: A reunion procession first officially held in 1909.
cards.evidence_claim: Smith says the first official Alumnae Parade was held in 1909; alumnae now dress in white, use colored ribbons for reunion classes and carry placards.
cards.source_title: Commencement & Ivy Day Traditions | Smith College
cards.access_notes: The parade is part of Smith’s Reunion and Ivy Day programming; check that year’s schedule.

cards.title: Notice the laurel chain leading the seniors
cards.subtitle: Carried by Junior Ushers on Ivy Day
cards.notes: Watch the Ivy Day procession for Junior Ushers carrying the shoulder-borne chain, which Smith notes is actually made of laurel leaves.
cards.short_summary: A deceptively named laurel-leaf procession chain.
cards.evidence_claim: Smith documents an Ivy Day ivy chain carried by Junior Ushers; the chain is made of laurel leaves and precedes the seniors in procession.
cards.source_title: Commencement & Ivy Day Traditions | Smith College
cards.access_notes: Visible within the Ivy Day procession during Commencement Weekend.

cards.title: Watch diplomas travel around the Quad
cards.subtitle: Post-Commencement graduating-class ritual
cards.notes: After Commencement, look toward the Laura Scales/Franklin King terrace as graduates form rings and pass diplomas until each reaches its owner.
cards.short_summary: A post-ceremony circle whose recorded history reaches 1911.
cards.evidence_claim: Smith traces the Diploma Circle to 1911 and says graduates form rings after Commencement, passing diplomas around until each graduate receives the correct one.
cards.source_title: Commencement & Ivy Day Traditions | Smith College
cards.access_notes: Takes place immediately following Smith’s Commencement ceremony.
